correctness.rationale: The all-dimension argument and its count hold. As an independent structural check, embed objects x as (x, parity(x)) and attributes y as (y, 1−parity(y)) in opposite bipartition classes of the (d+1)-cube. Incidences are then exactly cube edges, including x=y in the original context. Two distinct cube vertices have at most two common neighbors, ruling out five matched pairs. A four-scale is an induced crown graph K4,4 minus a perfect matching, hence a 3-cube. In a cube embedding the opposite edges of every 4-cycle have the same direction; applying this on the faces of the 3-cube identifies three fixed, distinct directions, so the image is a coordinate face. According as the appended bit varies or not, projection gives the coordinate-square or complementary parity-tetrahedron case, with unique witnesses. Thus the 3-face count is 2^(d−2) binom(d+1,3), including d=2. The Boolean-suborder implication is a bound, not a count.
